2	
3	Status: model-consensus target architecture and ongoing proof methodology. Do
4	not treat this as an implementation log.
5	
6	Consensus artifacts:
7	
8	- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-01/model-a-final.md`
9	- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-01/model-b-final.md`
10	- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-02/model-a-final.md`
11	- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-02/model-b-final.md`

16	
17	## Bottom Line
18	
19	The architecture is simple: Codex Dock must have one production truth path for
20	live state, and every important claim about freshness must be proven over time.
21	
22	The client must not be asked to guess whether a connected socket means current
23	data. The relay must own app-server decoding, card truth, freshness,
24	completeness, order, and stream liveness. The client renders that truth and
25	requests rebuilds when the relay's stream identity changes or falls behind.
26	
27	The testing strategy is also simple: static snapshots are useful, but they are
28	not proof that the app works. The proof of record is live convergence:
29	
30	```text
31	real or controlled app-server state changes
32	  -> relay projection and subscriptions
33	  -> Swift stream/session clients
34	  -> rendered iPhone UI samples over time
35	  -> retained machine-readable reports with lag budgets
36	```
37	
38	The repo already has much of the live-proof harness. The missing architecture is
39	that this proof is opt-in, unscheduled, ungated, and partly underspecified. That
40	is why stale-update bugs can ship while tests pass.
41	
42	## Canonical Principles
43	
44	### P1. One Owner Per Fact
45	
46	Every client-visible fact has exactly one production owner.
47	
48	| Fact | Canonical owner | Forbidden second owner |
49	| --- | --- | --- |
50	| Dock and Archive card existence | Relay `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams | Swift local metadata, diagnostics, preview fixtures, raw app-server routes |
51	| Card order and recency | Relay `orderKey` / `activityAtMs` | Swift timestamp inference, pins, row text, latest rendered message |
52	| Card freshness and completeness | Relay freshness/completeness fields | Socket connectivity, HTTP diagnostics, host test success |
53	| Human-only filtering | Relay human-started filter, with Swift defensive filter | Client-side list reconstruction from broad raw thread routes |
54	| Thread Detail history | `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus fully paged `thread/turns/list` | Dock cards, raw card summaries, partial resume payloads |
55	| Thread Detail liveness | Focused `thread/resume` session | Socket state alone |
56	| Local labels, rails, pins | Swift local metadata | Relay/card truth fields |
57	
58	Local metadata may decorate visible rows. It must never create a row, change
59	card order, mark data fresh, change status, change summary, or resurrect a row
60	that the relay no longer emits.
61	
62	### P2. Liveness Must Be Re-Proven
63	
64	A connected WebSocket is not proof that the data is current.
65	
66	Every stateful relay-owned stream or session must have an identity:
67	
68	- Dock and Archive streams: `epoch`, `seq`, and `stateGeneration`.
69	- Thread Detail live session: relay downstream session generation plus the
70	  active upstream `thread/resume` binding.
71	- Realtime transcription: transcription `sessionId` plus sequence acceptance.
72	
73	When that identity changes, the missing state must be rebuilt in an observable
74	way:
75	
76	- Dock and Archive must resubscribe or resync.
77	- Thread Detail must rehydrate from history before trusting live deltas again.
78	- The UI must show stale/partial/reconnecting when freshness is not proven.
79	
80	No production path may silently recover a relay upstream session while leaving
81	the phone thinking its old stream is still complete.
82	
83	### P3. Proof Is Over-Time Convergence
84	
85	Proof means the rendered client stays converged with actual source state over a
86	duration and within a lag budget.
87	
88	The following are not enough:
89	
90	- a static fixture that renders once;
91	- a fake Swift stream that manually yields a good payload;
92	- a one-shot `dock/subscribe`;
93	- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, or `/syncz`;
94	- a green `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` when the displayed sync proof
95	  skipped because its config file was absent.
96	
97	Those checks can be useful, but they are lower-tier evidence. They do not prove
98	the live system is current.
99	
100	## Target Architecture
101	
102	### Rule 1. Phone Uses Relay Only
103	
104	The phone connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not to the raw authenticated
105	app-server on `:4500`.
106	
107	Allowed normal phone paths:
108	
109	- relay WebSocket for `initialize`, `dock/*`, `archive/*`, Thread Detail,
110	  composer commands, server requests, and transcription;
111	- relay-provided host config such as `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`,
112	  `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`, LAN hostname, or LAN IP.
113	
114	Forbidden normal phone paths:
115	
116	- raw app-server `:4500`;
117	- raw app-server bearer tokens on device;
118	- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
119	  state routes used to rebuild cards;
120	- relay SQLite/debug/state routes as card truth.
121	
122	### Rule 2. Relay Owns Card Truth
123	
124	The relay is the only production card-truth owner for Dock and Archive.
125	
126	The relay owns:
127	
128	- app-server history reads;
129	- live loaded-session scans;
130	- human-started filtering;
131	- latest-activity proof;
132	- card normalization;
133	- SQLite materialization;
134	- stream sequence and snapshot generation;
135	- freshness and completeness;
136	- `dock/update` and `archive/update` deltas.
137	
138	Swift owns:
139	
140	- rendering;
141	- grouping/filtering/searching of relay rows;
142	- local decorative metadata;
143	- resync/resubscribe behavior when the relay stream contract says state is
144	  incomplete, stale, mismatched, or behind.
145	
146	Swift must not reconstruct card truth from Thread Detail history or local
147	metadata.
148	
149	### Rule 3. Relay Owns Recency
150	
151	Dock and Archive order are relay-owned. The client renders relay order.
152	
153	The client must not infer row recency from:
154	
155	- latest visible message;
156	- first message;
157	- pinned status;
158	- local label;
159	- local rail;
160	- Thread Detail events;
161	- raw timestamps from a side route.
162	
163	This prevents the same user-facing bug from reappearing under a new local
164	projection.
165	
166	### Rule 4. Thread Detail Uses One History Path
167	
168	Thread Detail history is:
169	
170	```text
171	thread/read includeTurns:false
172	  -> thread/turns/list until nextCursor is empty
173	  -> thread/resume excludeTurns:true
174	```
175	
176	For user-visible detail completeness, `thread/turns/list` must request
177	`itemsView:"full"` on the detail path.
178	
179	Important scoping rule:
180	
181	- Thread Detail history requests should use `itemsView:"full"`.
182	- Relay card-order activity proof calls should not use `itemsView:"full"`.
183	
184	The card-order proof needs turn activity timestamps and ordering proof. It does
185	not need full item bodies. Forcing full item bodies into relay card proof would
186	mix two separate concerns and increase payload cost.
187	
188	Current gap to close during implementation: `ThreadTurnsListParams` does not
189	currently carry `itemsView`, and relay `listThreadTurns` forwards params as-is.
190	The sync audit has a `--turn-items-view` flag, but the production detail path
191	does not currently send the field.
192	
193	### Rule 5. Stateful Recovery Must Be Observable
194	
195	Stateful paths cannot silently reconnect and keep old state.
196	
197	Dock and Archive:
198	
199	- reconnecting the transport is not enough;
200	- `initialize` replay is not enough;
201	- the subscription must be restored;
202	- if subscription continuity is not provable, the stream must resubscribe or
203	  fail into a visible rebuild path.
204	
205	Thread Detail:
206	
207	- if the downstream phone socket closes, Swift already rehydrates;
208	- if the relay loses and recreates the upstream `thread/resume` session, the
209	  phone must also observe a rebuild trigger.
210	
211	Consensus decision: close the downstream Thread Detail socket on relay upstream
212	recovery unless the app-server provides a proven replay guarantee.
213	
214	Why close the downstream socket now:
215	
216	- Swift already has a tested reconnect/rehydrate path.
217	- It avoids adding a new protocol message before the architecture is stable.
218	- It prevents the exact stale-detail failure shape: relay recovered upstream,
219	  phone stayed connected, and missed history was never replayed.
220	
221	Sanctioned future alternative:
222	
223	- a `detail/resync` or equivalent notification may exist later only if it is
224	  `threadId`-stamped, generation-stamped, added to the relay allow-list, added
225	  to Swift DTO handling, added to proof tests, and documented here in the same
226	  change.
227	
228	Until then, invisible upstream recovery is forbidden.
229	
230	### Rule 6. Heartbeat Is Real Contract
231	
232	Heartbeat is not decorative. It is the stream liveness signal.
233	
234	The repo already claims heartbeat in schema, Swift behavior, tests, and README.
235	The target architecture makes it real instead of leaving a dead contract.
236	
237	Relay should emit periodic `kind:"heartbeat"` `dock/update` messages with:
238	
239	- `schemaVersion`;
240	- `view`;
241	- `epoch`;
242	- `seq`;
243	- `stateGeneration`;
244	- `freshness`;
245	- `lastSyncAt` or equivalent freshness timestamp;
246	- no row changes.
247	
248	The client uses heartbeat to detect:
249	
250	- connected-but-unsubscribed streams;
251	- streams whose relay state is stale even though the socket is open;
252	- missing updates beyond a bounded timeout.
253	
254	Heartbeat must never mark failed data fresh. It may keep the transport alive,
255	but freshness remains a relay data claim.
256	
257	Bounded implementation parameter:
258	
259	- heartbeat cadence should align with relay reconcile timing, roughly the
260	  reconcile interval or a small multiple;
261	- client stale timeout should be a small multiple of heartbeat cadence;
262	- exact values belong in constants, not scattered call sites.
263	
264	### Rule 7. Freshness Fails Closed
265	
266	If the relay cannot prove a source is current, client-visible freshness must be
267	stale or partial, not fresh.
268	
269	This applies to:
270	
271	- raw app-server history failures;
272	- live endpoint failures;
273	- live lease scan failures;
274	- validation failures during human-started filtering;
275	- repeated turn cursors;
276	- schema or sequence mismatch;
277	- incomplete windows;
278	- failed archive reconciliation.
279	
280	Current gap to close during implementation: live endpoint failures can be
281	counted and then effectively hidden by history completeness. The target rule is
282	that live-scope probe failure marks the relevant scope stale/incomplete and the
283	client renders that state.
284	
285	### Rule 8. Snapshots Cannot Move State Backward
286	
287	Snapshots are full replacements, but they are not allowed to overwrite newer
288	state with older state.
289	
290	The relay already has monotonic stream sequence material:
291	
292	- `seq`;
293	- `stateGeneration`;
294	- `epoch`;
295	- `schemaVersion`.
296	
297	Swift must reject stale compatible snapshots when their generation is older
298	than the current host/view state. A compatible schema is not enough.
299	
300	Current gap to close during implementation: Swift currently applies compatible
301	snapshots without a stale-generation guard.
302	
303	### Rule 9. Archive Is A First-Class View
304	
305	Archive and Dock are separate views with related but distinct freshness.
306	
307	Archive/unarchive mutations must reconcile and publish both affected views:
308	
309	- Dock view;
310	- Archive view.
311	
312	Archive freshness must not be accidentally coupled to Dock freshness such that
313	one scope can stale or freshen the other without proof.
314	
315	Current gap to close during implementation: archive mutation scheduling is
316	drift-prone because the mutation ingestion path schedules generic reconciliation
317	but does not make Archive convergence a first-class invariant.
318

344	
345	## Forbidden Side Doors
346	
347	These are not allowed to count as production card truth or live freshness proof:
348	
349	- phone calls to raw `:4500`;
350	- phone-side raw bearer tokens;
351	- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
352	  state routes;
353	- relay debug/state/diagnostic routes as list truth;
354	- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, `/syncz` as stream freshness;
355	- one-shot host connection tests as Dock Home stream health;
356	- `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO` as live proof;
357	- Swift preview rows as evidence;
358	- local metadata as card existence/order/status/freshness truth;
359	- static JSON fixtures as over-time update proof;
360	- tests that preserve a retired route "for coverage";
361	- docs that recommend deleted scripts or unsupported flags;
362	- proof commands that skip and still let the run be interpreted as freshness
363	  proof.
364	
365	Important: a skipped over-time proof is itself a side door. It lets a green
366	test run masquerade as a live freshness pass.
367	
368	## Edge And Exception Matrix
369	
370	| Scenario | Required behavior | Proof surface |
371	| --- | --- | --- |
372	| Dock WebSocket reconnects | `dock/subscribe` is restored or stream fails into visible rebuild | Swift stream test plus real relay soak |
373	| `dock/update` params missing | Treat as stream corruption; resync/fail, not silent ignore | Swift unit plus relay malformed update test |
374	| Sequence gap | Request `dock/resync` and converge | Swift stream test plus relay integration |
375	| Epoch mismatch | Request resync and do not apply stale delta | Swift stream test |
376	| Schema mismatch | Request resync/fail loudly | Swift stream test plus contract test |
377	| Older compatible snapshot | Reject if generation is older than current state | Swift unit plus relay delayed snapshot scenario |
378	| Heartbeat arrives | Update liveness/freshness without row mutation | Swift unit plus relay integration |
379	| Heartbeat stops | Mark stream stale/reconnect within timeout | controlled simulator scenario |
380	| Raw app-server history down | Relay marks scope stale/partial; UI does not claim fresh | relay integration plus UI proof |
381	| Live endpoint down | Live scope fails closed; UI shows stale/partial | controlled `source-refresh` / live failure scenario |
382	| Cold relay SQLite | UI can show empty/partial only with explicit freshness state | relay integration |
383	| Stale SQLite | Reconcile or show stale; do not present old cache as fresh | soak comparing long-lived stream vs fresh snapshot |
384	| Partial window | UI marks partial and catch-up completes or restarts | Swift unit plus controlled large-list scenario |
385	| Large delta fallback | Snapshot fallback preserves monotonic generation | relay integration plus Swift table test |
386	| Duplicate card IDs | Reject safely; do not crash through `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` | Swift unit |
387	| Non-human upsert for human card | Delete/resync or reject; do not leave stale human card | relay contract plus Swift table test |
388	| Archive mutation | Dock and Archive both reconcile and publish relevant updates | relay integration plus UI archive scenario |
389	| Archive failure | UI surfaces action failure and does not fabricate row state | Swift store test plus relay scenario |
390	| Host alias/identity change | Resolve configured/stream/logical host identity without duplicating rows | Swift host identity tests |
391	| Relay host ID changes cache scope | Prune or invalidate old host rows explicitly | relay state-store test |
392	| Thread Detail initial load | `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, then `thread/resume` | ThreadDetailStore tests plus sync audit detail probe |
393	| Thread Detail repeated cursor | Fail loudly; do not spin or silently truncate | ThreadDetailStore test |
394	| Thread Detail upstream recovery | Close downstream or send sanctioned resync; Swift rehydrates | relay integration plus UI detail scenario |
395	| Missing `threadId` in detail notification | Drop or classify explicitly; request-card resolution must not vanish silently | ThreadDetailStore test |
396	| Multiple active turns | Preserve all visible activity or define single-active-turn UI explicitly | Thread detail event test |
397	| Server request stale generation | Reject response from stale generation | relay integration |
398	| `serverRequest/resolved` | Clear matching request card; define missing-thread behavior | ThreadDetailStore test plus controlled fixture |
399	| Background/foreground | Rehydrate or resync; do not trust stale in-memory state | Swift lifecycle test plus simulator proof |
400	| Realtime transcription disconnect | Transcription state closes without mutating Dock/Detail truth | voice tests |
401	| Config rewrite while app runs | Existing streams close/reload or UI exposes old config explicitly | host registry/store test |
402	| Docs command drift | Doc command gate fails on unsupported flags/deleted scripts | doc-command gate |

404	## Testing Methodology
405	
406	The proof system has six tiers. Lower tiers are necessary, but they cannot
407	replace higher tiers.
408	
409	### Tier A. Contract And Drift Gates
410	
411	Purpose: keep protocol surfaces aligned before runtime.
412	
413	Required gates:
414	
415	- current card contract checks;
416	- route registry/dispatch parity;
417	- Swift `AppServerMethods` parity with allowed relay routes;
418	- schema version parity across JSON schema, relay emission, and Swift constants;
419	- generated DTO staleness check;
420	- proof-result schema validation;
421	- executable doc-command gate.
422	
423	Candidate commands:
424	
425	```bash
426	rtk npm run contract:check
427	rtk npm run test:relay
428	```
429	
430	New target direction: add one CI-safe aggregate target that runs all fast drift
431	gates without simulator or physical device dependency.
432	
433	### Tier B. Swift State Tests
434	
435	Purpose: prove Swift state machines handle known events correctly.
436	
437	These tests can use fake streams, but they must be labeled as merge/state proof,
438	not live proof.
439	
440	Coverage required:
441	
442	- snapshot, delta, heartbeat;
443	- schema/epoch/sequence mismatch;
444	- resync behavior;
445	- stale snapshot rejection;
446	- duplicate card IDs;
447	- partial window catch-up;
448	- missing update params;
449	- Thread Detail pagination;
450	- Thread Detail rehydrate on reconnect and foreground;
451	- server request and resolution behavior;
452	- archive action state transitions.
453	
454	Representative commands:
455	
456	```bash
457	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
458	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
459	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
460	```
461	
462	Interpretation rule: passing Tier B means Swift can handle supplied events. It
463	does not prove real relay delivery over time.
464	
465	### Tier C. Relay Integration Tests
466	
467	Purpose: prove real relay behavior with fake or controlled upstreams.
468	
469	Coverage required:
470	
471	- `dock/subscribe` returns canonical snapshot;
472	- server state mutation emits `dock/update`;
473	- multi-subscriber updates;
474	- delete-only delta;
475	- `dock/resync`;
476	- Archive mutation emits Dock and Archive convergence;
477	- live failure fails closed;
478	- heartbeat is emitted;
479	- stale snapshot/generation behavior;
480	- route allow-list rejects unsupported paths.
481	
482	Representative command:
483	
484	```bash
485	rtk npm run test:relay
486	```
487	
488	Interpretation rule: passing Tier C proves relay protocol behavior below the UI.
489	It does not prove the Swift app rendered the update.
490	
491	### Tier D. Real Relay Client-Path Soak
492	
493	Purpose: prove long-lived relay streams stay converged with fresh snapshots over
494	time.
495	
496	Required properties:
497	
498	- long-lived `dock/subscribe`;
499	- periodic fresh `dock/subscribe`;
500	- comparison of long-lived stream state against fresh snapshot;
501	- forced `dock/resync`;
502	- detail probe that runs `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, and
503	  `thread/resume`;
504	- lag budget;
505	- retained JSON and Markdown reports.
506	
507	Representative command family:
508	
509	```bash
510	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs --mode soak --client-path-only --force-dock-resync --max-stream-lag-ms 2000
511	```
512	
513	Current doc drift to fix during implementation: older docs mention unsupported
514	or deleted command surfaces such as `--exhaustive` and deleted parity scripts.
515	The doc-command gate must make that impossible to miss.
516	
517	### Tier E. Simulator Displayed-UI Proof
518	
519	Purpose: prove the iPhone simulator actually displays the live state over time.
520	
521	Required properties:
522	
523	- app launched without `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO`;
524	- real relay-backed or controlled relay-backed rows;
525	- UI samples over a duration;
526	- route evidence from relay side;
527	- row-level and detail-level UI samples;
528	- transition coverage;
529	- lag budget;
530	- retained machine-readable report.
531	
532	Representative commands:
533	
534	```bash
535	rtk make sim-ui-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
536	rtk make sim-ui-scenario-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
537	rtk make sim-ui-controlled-scenario-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
538	rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof SIM='iPhone 17' SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_PASSES=2 MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000
539	```
540	
541	Interpretation rule: `CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests` skipping because
542	`/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-sim-ui-sync-config.json` is absent is not proof.
543	For update-path changes, this tier must run or be explicitly reported as
544	blocked by missing simulator/Xcode infrastructure.
545	
546	### Tier F. Physical Phone Proof
547	
548	Purpose: prove the real phone path, including network profile and saved host
549	configuration.
550	
551	Representative commands:
552	
553	```bash
554	rtk make iphone-17-pro
555	rtk make device-config-verify DEVICE=CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E
556	rtk make device-logs DEVICE=CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E
557	```
558	
559	Interpretation rule: simulator proof is not physical phone proof. Physical
560	completion requires a real installed app connected through the intended relay
561	host path.
562	
563	## Ongoing Cadence
564	
565	The methodology must run continuously enough to catch drift before manual use.
566	
567	Recommended cadence:
568	
569	| Trigger | Required proof |
570	| --- | --- |
571	| Every source change in update-path files | Tier A plus affected Tier B/C |
572	| Relay protocol, card DTO, stream, Thread Detail, or proof harness change | Tier A/B/C plus Tier E controlled matrix |
573	| Daily/nightly on a capable Mac | Tier D soak plus Tier E controlled matrix |
574	| Before claiming simulator behavior fixed | Tier E on `iPhone 17` |
575	| Before claiming phone behavior fixed | Tier F |
576	| Before changing docs/runbooks | Doc-command gate plus affected referenced commands in dry-run or real mode |
577	
578	Update-path files include:
579	
580	- `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs`;
581	- `contract/dock/**`;
582	- `CodexDock/AppServer/**`;
583	- `CodexDock/State/**`;
584	- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/**`;
585	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/**`;
586	- `CodexDockUITests/**`;
587	- `Makefile`;
588	- live-update docs and runbooks.
589	
590	## Proof Acceptance Rules
591	
592	Every proof report should classify the run as one of:
593	
594	- `pass`: required routes, transitions, UI samples, freshness states, and lag
595	  budgets passed.
596	- `fail`: the proof ran and found divergence, stale UI, missing route evidence,
597	  missing transition, or lag over budget.
598	- `blocked`: infrastructure was unavailable, such as no simulator, no relay,
599	  no app-server, missing signing, or physical device unavailable.
600	- `outside-contract`: the run used scripted fixtures, debug env vars, preview
601	  rows, raw app-server path, or another forbidden proof route.
602	
603	No proof may be counted as pass if:
604	
605	- it skipped;
606	- it had no route evidence;
607	- it only compared static snapshots;
608	- it lacked a retained report;
609	- it did not validate its report schema;
610	- it ignored stale/partial freshness;
611	- it did not sample over time.
612	
613	Required retained report fields:
614	
615	- `schemaVersion`;
616	- `kind`;
617	- `startedAt`;
618	- `endedAt`;
619	- `durationMs`;
620	- source host(s);
621	- app/server/relay build identifiers where available;
622	- scenario name(s);
623	- route counts;
624	- sampled transitions;
625	- UI sample count;
626	- max observed lag;
627	- lag budget;
628	- freshness states;
629	- pass/fail findings;
630	- artifact paths.
631	
632	## Drift Gates
633	
634	### Gate 1. Route Registry And Dispatch Parity
635	
636	The relay dispatch switch, relay route registry/observability config, Swift
637	route names, and docs must agree.
638	
639	A route must not be silently valid because a helper auto-created an unregistered
640	route. New routes are allowed only when they update:
641	
642	- relay dispatch;
643	- route registry/observability;
644	- Swift method constants/DTOs if phone-visible;
645	- tests;
646	- docs.
647	
648	### Gate 2. Schema Version And DTO Parity
649	
650	These values must move together:
651	
652	- JSON schema `schemaVersion`;
653	- relay emitted `schemaVersion`;
654	- Swift `CodexDockConstants.Dock.streamSchemaVersion`;
655	- generated Swift DTOs;
656	- tests and fixtures.
657	
658	Generated DTO staleness is a build failure, not a review note.
659	
660	### Gate 3. Executable Doc Commands
661	
662	Docs that name runnable commands must not drift from real CLIs.
663	
664	This gate should catch:
665	
666	- unsupported flags such as stale `--exhaustive`;
667	- deleted scripts such as stale parity helpers;
668	- Makefile target renames;
669	- commands that require env/config but do not say so;
670	- commands that skip by default while being described as proof.
671	
672	### Gate 4. Proof Result Schemas
673	
674	Proof reports need schemas just like card DTOs.
675	
676	Create and enforce schemas for:
677	
678	- relay sync audit reports;
679	- simulator UI sync proof reports;
680	- controlled simulator fixture reports;
681	- controlled simulator matrix reports.
682	
683	The current reports have `schemaVersion` and `kind`, but no schema file guards
684	their shape. That means proof consumers and docs can drift.
685	
686	### Gate 5. Heartbeat Contract
687	
688	If schema, README, Swift tests, or docs say heartbeat exists, relay must emit it.
689	
690	The gate must fail if:
691	
692	- heartbeat is documented but not emitted;
693	- heartbeat is emitted but schema/DTO/tests do not allow it;
694	- heartbeat marks stale data fresh;
695	- client does not timeout missing heartbeat.
696	
697	## UX Freshness Contract
698	
699	The UI should make these states visible and distinct:
700	
701	| State | Meaning |
702	| --- | --- |
703	| Fresh | Relay has current proof for this view/scope. |
704	| Partial | Relay has usable rows but incomplete proof/window/source coverage. |
705	| Stale | Relay has old rows but cannot prove current source state. |
706	| Reconnecting | Stateful stream/session identity is being rebuilt. |
707	| Offline | No usable relay path is currently available. |
708	| Blocked | Command/test/proof could not run because infrastructure is missing. |
709	
710	Global connectivity may summarize transport reachability, but it must not hide
711	stale stream freshness. A small "online" badge is misleading if the rows are a
712	day old.
713	
714	## Rejected Alternatives
715	
716	### Static Fixtures As Proof Of Record
717	
718	Rejected because they prove only merge/render behavior for supplied data. They
719	do not prove that current Codex work reaches the phone.
720	
721	### Client-Inferred Recency
722	
723	Rejected because it creates a second card-truth path and reintroduces ordering
724	bugs.
725	
726	### Diagnostics As Freshness
727	
728	Rejected because route health can be green while the long-lived stream is
729	unsubscribed or stale.
730	
731	### New Parallel Test Framework
732	
733	Rejected because the repo already contains the core live-proof harness. The
734	right move is to make it mandatory, scheduled, schema-validated, retained, and
735	drift-gated.
736	
737	### Invisible Thread Detail Upstream Recovery
738	
739	Rejected because it is the exact stale-detail failure mode.
740	
741	### Delete Heartbeat Without Replacement
742	
743	Rejected because it leaves socket connectivity as the liveness signal. Removing
744	heartbeat is acceptable only if replaced by an equally strong client-visible
745	watchdog contract. Making heartbeat real is cleaner because the schema and
746	Swift already know about it.
747	
748	### Add `detail/resync` Immediately
749	
750	Rejected for now because downstream close reuses existing Swift rehydrate
751	behavior. `detail/resync` is the sanctioned future evolution only if full
752	evidence shows downstream close is too expensive.
753	
754	## Implementation Plan Outline
755	
756	This document does not implement these changes. A future implementation plan
757	should be phased like this:
758	
759	1. Update docs/runbooks so command references are executable and this document
760	   is the canonical live-update architecture reference.
761	2. Add drift gates that are CI-safe and do not require simulator/device.
762	3. Make heartbeat real or remove every heartbeat claim and replace it with an
763	   equivalent explicit watchdog. Consensus recommendation is make heartbeat
764	   real.
765	4. Fix stateful recovery: Dock/Archive resubscribe after reconnect and Thread
766	   Detail upstream recovery closes downstream or triggers sanctioned rehydrate.
767	5. Add snapshot generation rejection in Swift.
768	6. Make live failures fail closed in relay freshness.
769	7. Make Archive reconciliation first-class after archive/unarchive.
770	8. Add `itemsView:"full"` to Thread Detail history and proof paths, scoped only
771	   to detail.
772	9. Add proof-result schemas and validate retained reports.
773	10. Make update-path changes require the controlled simulator matrix and retain
774	    reports.
775	11. Add scheduled soak/matrix runs where infrastructure exists.
776	12. Add physical phone proof as the completion gate for phone claims.
777	
778	Each phase must remove or converge old paths. Do not leave a retired side door
779	alive for tests.
780	
781	## Canonical Documentation Relationship
782	
783	This document is the canonical target architecture and ongoing methodology for
784	live updates.
785	
786	Relationship to other docs:
787	
788	- `CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md` remains
789	  the deep protocol and bug appendix.
790	- `CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md` remains
791	  historical evidence for data-contract drift.
792	- Existing exhaustive sync runbooks/test plans should be updated to remove
793	  stale commands and align with this methodology.
794	- README should align with heartbeat reality after implementation.
795	
796	If another doc disagrees with this target architecture, this doc wins for
797	live-update architecture intent until a newer explicitly canonical reference
798	replaces it.
799	
800	## Final Consensus Statement
801	
802	Opus 4.8 max and GPT-5.5 xhigh converged on the same architecture:
803	
804	- one canonical production truth path;
805	- relay-owned card truth and freshness;
806	- observable rebuild on stateful identity changes;
807	- heartbeat as real liveness contract;
808	- detail history with `itemsView:"full"` only on the detail path;
809	- live failures fail closed;
810	- snapshots cannot move state backward;
811	- Archive is a first-class stream view;
812	- live proof over time is mandatory, retained, scheduled, schema-validated, and
813	  gated for update-path changes.
814	
815	The remaining open value, heartbeat cadence/timeout, is an implementation
816	parameter. It does not change the architecture.

# Codex Dock Live Update Architecture And Testing Reference - 2026-06-01

Status: model-consensus target architecture and ongoing proof methodology. Do
not treat this as an implementation log.

Consensus artifacts:

- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-01/model-a-final.md`
- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-01/model-b-final.md`
- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-02/model-a-final.md`
- `.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-live-update-architecture-20260601T001659Z/round-02/model-b-final.md`

Primary input:

- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md`

## Bottom Line

The architecture is simple: Codex Dock must have one production truth path for
live state, and every important claim about freshness must be proven over time.

The client must not be asked to guess whether a connected socket means current
data. The relay must own app-server decoding, card truth, freshness,
completeness, order, and stream liveness. The client renders that truth and
requests rebuilds when the relay's stream identity changes or falls behind.

The testing strategy is also simple: static snapshots are useful, but they are
not proof that the app works. The proof of record is live convergence:

```text
real or controlled app-server state changes
  -> relay projection and subscriptions
  -> Swift stream/session clients
  -> rendered iPhone UI samples over time
  -> retained machine-readable reports with lag budgets
```

The repo already has much of the live-proof harness. The missing architecture is
that this proof is opt-in, unscheduled, ungated, and partly underspecified. That
is why stale-update bugs can ship while tests pass.

## Canonical Principles

### P1. One Owner Per Fact

Every client-visible fact has exactly one production owner.

| Fact | Canonical owner | Forbidden second owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dock and Archive card existence | Relay `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams | Swift local metadata, diagnostics, preview fixtures, raw app-server routes |
| Card order and recency | Relay `orderKey` / `activityAtMs` | Swift timestamp inference, pins, row text, latest rendered message |
| Card freshness and completeness | Relay freshness/completeness fields | Socket connectivity, HTTP diagnostics, host test success |
| Human-only filtering | Relay human-started filter, with Swift defensive filter | Client-side list reconstruction from broad raw thread routes |
| Thread Detail history | `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus fully paged `thread/turns/list` | Dock cards, raw card summaries, partial resume payloads |
| Thread Detail liveness | Focused `thread/resume` session | Socket state alone |
| Local labels, rails, pins | Swift local metadata | Relay/card truth fields |

Local metadata may decorate visible rows. It must never create a row, change
card order, mark data fresh, change status, change summary, or resurrect a row
that the relay no longer emits.

### P2. Liveness Must Be Re-Proven

A connected WebSocket is not proof that the data is current.

Every stateful relay-owned stream or session must have an identity:

- Dock and Archive streams: `epoch`, `seq`, and `stateGeneration`.
- Thread Detail live session: relay downstream session generation plus the
  active upstream `thread/resume` binding.
- Realtime transcription: transcription `sessionId` plus sequence acceptance.

When that identity changes, the missing state must be rebuilt in an observable
way:

- Dock and Archive must resubscribe or resync.
- Thread Detail must rehydrate from history before trusting live deltas again.
- The UI must show stale/partial/reconnecting when freshness is not proven.

No production path may silently recover a relay upstream session while leaving
the phone thinking its old stream is still complete.

### P3. Proof Is Over-Time Convergence

Proof means the rendered client stays converged with actual source state over a
duration and within a lag budget.

The following are not enough:

- a static fixture that renders once;
- a fake Swift stream that manually yields a good payload;
- a one-shot `dock/subscribe`;
- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, or `/syncz`;
- a green `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` when the displayed sync proof
  skipped because its config file was absent.

Those checks can be useful, but they are lower-tier evidence. They do not prove
the live system is current.

## Target Architecture

### Rule 1. Phone Uses Relay Only

The phone connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not to the raw authenticated
app-server on `:4500`.

Allowed normal phone paths:

- relay WebSocket for `initialize`, `dock/*`, `archive/*`, Thread Detail,
  composer commands, server requests, and transcription;
- relay-provided host config such as `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`,
  `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`, LAN hostname, or LAN IP.

Forbidden normal phone paths:

- raw app-server `:4500`;
- raw app-server bearer tokens on device;
- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
  state routes used to rebuild cards;
- relay SQLite/debug/state routes as card truth.

### Rule 2. Relay Owns Card Truth

The relay is the only production card-truth owner for Dock and Archive.

The relay owns:

- app-server history reads;
- live loaded-session scans;
- human-started filtering;
- latest-activity proof;
- card normalization;
- SQLite materialization;
- stream sequence and snapshot generation;
- freshness and completeness;
- `dock/update` and `archive/update` deltas.

Swift owns:

- rendering;
- grouping/filtering/searching of relay rows;
- local decorative metadata;
- resync/resubscribe behavior when the relay stream contract says state is
  incomplete, stale, mismatched, or behind.

Swift must not reconstruct card truth from Thread Detail history or local
metadata.

### Rule 3. Relay Owns Recency

Dock and Archive order are relay-owned. The client renders relay order.

The client must not infer row recency from:

- latest visible message;
- first message;
- pinned status;
- local label;
- local rail;
- Thread Detail events;
- raw timestamps from a side route.

This prevents the same user-facing bug from reappearing under a new local
projection.

### Rule 4. Thread Detail Uses One History Path

Thread Detail history is:

```text
thread/read includeTurns:false
  -> thread/turns/list until nextCursor is empty
  -> thread/resume excludeTurns:true
```

For user-visible detail completeness, `thread/turns/list` must request
`itemsView:"full"` on the detail path.

Important scoping rule:

- Thread Detail history requests should use `itemsView:"full"`.
- Relay card-order activity proof calls should not use `itemsView:"full"`.

The card-order proof needs turn activity timestamps and ordering proof. It does
not need full item bodies. Forcing full item bodies into relay card proof would
mix two separate concerns and increase payload cost.

Current gap to close during implementation: `ThreadTurnsListParams` does not
currently carry `itemsView`, and relay `listThreadTurns` forwards params as-is.
The sync audit has a `--turn-items-view` flag, but the production detail path
does not currently send the field.

### Rule 5. Stateful Recovery Must Be Observable

Stateful paths cannot silently reconnect and keep old state.

Dock and Archive:

- reconnecting the transport is not enough;
- `initialize` replay is not enough;
- the subscription must be restored;
- if subscription continuity is not provable, the stream must resubscribe or
  fail into a visible rebuild path.

Thread Detail:

- if the downstream phone socket closes, Swift already rehydrates;
- if the relay loses and recreates the upstream `thread/resume` session, the
  phone must also observe a rebuild trigger.

Consensus decision: close the downstream Thread Detail socket on relay upstream
recovery unless the app-server provides a proven replay guarantee.

Why close the downstream socket now:

- Swift already has a tested reconnect/rehydrate path.
- It avoids adding a new protocol message before the architecture is stable.
- It prevents the exact stale-detail failure shape: relay recovered upstream,
  phone stayed connected, and missed history was never replayed.

Sanctioned future alternative:

- a `detail/resync` or equivalent notification may exist later only if it is
  `threadId`-stamped, generation-stamped, added to the relay allow-list, added
  to Swift DTO handling, added to proof tests, and documented here in the same
  change.

Until then, invisible upstream recovery is forbidden.

### Rule 6. Heartbeat Is Real Contract

Heartbeat is not decorative. It is the stream liveness signal.

The repo already claims heartbeat in schema, Swift behavior, tests, and README.
The target architecture makes it real instead of leaving a dead contract.

Relay should emit periodic `kind:"heartbeat"` `dock/update` messages with:

- `schemaVersion`;
- `view`;
- `epoch`;
- `seq`;
- `stateGeneration`;
- `freshness`;
- `lastSyncAt` or equivalent freshness timestamp;
- no row changes.

The client uses heartbeat to detect:

- connected-but-unsubscribed streams;
- streams whose relay state is stale even though the socket is open;
- missing updates beyond a bounded timeout.

Heartbeat must never mark failed data fresh. It may keep the transport alive,
but freshness remains a relay data claim.

Bounded implementation parameter:

- heartbeat cadence should align with relay reconcile timing, roughly the
  reconcile interval or a small multiple;
- client stale timeout should be a small multiple of heartbeat cadence;
- exact values belong in constants, not scattered call sites.

### Rule 7. Freshness Fails Closed

If the relay cannot prove a source is current, client-visible freshness must be
stale or partial, not fresh.

This applies to:

- raw app-server history failures;
- live endpoint failures;
- live lease scan failures;
- validation failures during human-started filtering;
- repeated turn cursors;
- schema or sequence mismatch;
- incomplete windows;
- failed archive reconciliation.

Current gap to close during implementation: live endpoint failures can be
counted and then effectively hidden by history completeness. The target rule is
that live-scope probe failure marks the relevant scope stale/incomplete and the
client renders that state.

### Rule 8. Snapshots Cannot Move State Backward

Snapshots are full replacements, but they are not allowed to overwrite newer
state with older state.

The relay already has monotonic stream sequence material:

- `seq`;
- `stateGeneration`;
- `epoch`;
- `schemaVersion`.

Swift must reject stale compatible snapshots when their generation is older
than the current host/view state. A compatible schema is not enough.

Current gap to close during implementation: Swift currently applies compatible
snapshots without a stale-generation guard.

### Rule 9. Archive Is A First-Class View

Archive and Dock are separate views with related but distinct freshness.

Archive/unarchive mutations must reconcile and publish both affected views:

- Dock view;
- Archive view.

Archive freshness must not be accidentally coupled to Dock freshness such that
one scope can stale or freshen the other without proof.

Current gap to close during implementation: archive mutation scheduling is
drift-prone because the mutation ingestion path schedules generic reconciliation
but does not make Archive convergence a first-class invariant.

## Owner Map

| Surface | Canonical owner |
| --- | --- |
| Relay route dispatch | `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` |
| Swift route names | `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerMethods.swift` |
| Dock card wire schema | `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` |
| Generated Swift card DTO | `CodexDock/AppServer/DockThreadCardDTO.swift` |
| Card contract generation/check | `scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs`, `scripts/check-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs` |
| Relay card projection | `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs` |
| Swift Dock stream client | `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift` |
| Swift Dock state | `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`, `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`, `CodexDock/Dock/DockScreenStore.swift` |
| Thread Detail session | `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadDetailSession.swift` |
| Thread Detail state | `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift`, `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift` |
| Connectivity display | `CodexDock/Connectivity/**`, `CodexDock/Features/Dock/**` |
| Real relay client-path proof | `scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs` |
| Simulator displayed UI proof | `CodexDockUITests/CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests.swift`, `scripts/dock-relay-simulator-ui-sync-proof.mjs` |
| Controlled simulator fixture | `scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-fixture.mjs` |
| Controlled matrix report | `scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-matrix.mjs` |
| Makefile proof entrypoints | `Makefile` |
| Product/runbook docs | `README.md`, docs listed in this file |

New architecture should extend these owners. It should not create a parallel
route map, parallel schema, parallel fixture framework, or parallel proof
report language unless the existing owner demonstrably cannot absorb it.

## Forbidden Side Doors

These are not allowed to count as production card truth or live freshness proof:

- phone calls to raw `:4500`;
- phone-side raw bearer tokens;
- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
  state routes;
- relay debug/state/diagnostic routes as list truth;
- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, `/syncz` as stream freshness;
- one-shot host connection tests as Dock Home stream health;
- `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO` as live proof;
- Swift preview rows as evidence;
- local metadata as card existence/order/status/freshness truth;
- static JSON fixtures as over-time update proof;
- tests that preserve a retired route "for coverage";
- docs that recommend deleted scripts or unsupported flags;
- proof commands that skip and still let the run be interpreted as freshness
  proof.

Important: a skipped over-time proof is itself a side door. It lets a green
test run masquerade as a live freshness pass.

## Edge And Exception Matrix

| Scenario | Required behavior | Proof surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dock WebSocket reconnects | `dock/subscribe` is restored or stream fails into visible rebuild | Swift stream test plus real relay soak |
| `dock/update` params missing | Treat as stream corruption; resync/fail, not silent ignore | Swift unit plus relay malformed update test |
| Sequence gap | Request `dock/resync` and converge | Swift stream test plus relay integration |
| Epoch mismatch | Request resync and do not apply stale delta | Swift stream test |
| Schema mismatch | Request resync/fail loudly | Swift stream test plus contract test |
| Older compatible snapshot | Reject if generation is older than current state | Swift unit plus relay delayed snapshot scenario |
| Heartbeat arrives | Update liveness/freshness without row mutation | Swift unit plus relay integration |
| Heartbeat stops | Mark stream stale/reconnect within timeout | controlled simulator scenario |
| Raw app-server history down | Relay marks scope stale/partial; UI does not claim fresh | relay integration plus UI proof |
| Live endpoint down | Live scope fails closed; UI shows stale/partial | controlled `source-refresh` / live failure scenario |
| Cold relay SQLite | UI can show empty/partial only with explicit freshness state | relay integration |
| Stale SQLite | Reconcile or show stale; do not present old cache as fresh | soak comparing long-lived stream vs fresh snapshot |
| Partial window | UI marks partial and catch-up completes or restarts | Swift unit plus controlled large-list scenario |
| Large delta fallback | Snapshot fallback preserves monotonic generation | relay integration plus Swift table test |
| Duplicate card IDs | Reject safely; do not crash through `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` | Swift unit |
| Non-human upsert for human card | Delete/resync or reject; do not leave stale human card | relay contract plus Swift table test |
| Archive mutation | Dock and Archive both reconcile and publish relevant updates | relay integration plus UI archive scenario |
| Archive failure | UI surfaces action failure and does not fabricate row state | Swift store test plus relay scenario |
| Host alias/identity change | Resolve configured/stream/logical host identity without duplicating rows | Swift host identity tests |
| Relay host ID changes cache scope | Prune or invalidate old host rows explicitly | relay state-store test |
| Thread Detail initial load | `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, then `thread/resume` | ThreadDetailStore tests plus sync audit detail probe |
| Thread Detail repeated cursor | Fail loudly; do not spin or silently truncate | ThreadDetailStore test |
| Thread Detail upstream recovery | Close downstream or send sanctioned resync; Swift rehydrates | relay integration plus UI detail scenario |
| Missing `threadId` in detail notification | Drop or classify explicitly; request-card resolution must not vanish silently | ThreadDetailStore test |
| Multiple active turns | Preserve all visible activity or define single-active-turn UI explicitly | Thread detail event test |
| Server request stale generation | Reject response from stale generation | relay integration |
| `serverRequest/resolved` | Clear matching request card; define missing-thread behavior | ThreadDetailStore test plus controlled fixture |
| Background/foreground | Rehydrate or resync; do not trust stale in-memory state | Swift lifecycle test plus simulator proof |
| Realtime transcription disconnect | Transcription state closes without mutating Dock/Detail truth | voice tests |
| Config rewrite while app runs | Existing streams close/reload or UI exposes old config explicitly | host registry/store test |
| Docs command drift | Doc command gate fails on unsupported flags/deleted scripts | doc-command gate |

## Testing Methodology

The proof system has six tiers. Lower tiers are necessary, but they cannot
replace higher tiers.

### Tier A. Contract And Drift Gates

Purpose: keep protocol surfaces aligned before runtime.

Required gates:

- current card contract checks;
- route registry/dispatch parity;
- Swift `AppServerMethods` parity with allowed relay routes;
- schema version parity across JSON schema, relay emission, and Swift constants;
- generated DTO staleness check;
- proof-result schema validation;
- executable doc-command gate.

Candidate commands:

```bash
rtk npm run contract:check
rtk npm run test:relay
```

New target direction: add one CI-safe aggregate target that runs all fast drift
gates without simulator or physical device dependency.

### Tier B. Swift State Tests

Purpose: prove Swift state machines handle known events correctly.

These tests can use fake streams, but they must be labeled as merge/state proof,
not live proof.

Coverage required:

- snapshot, delta, heartbeat;
- schema/epoch/sequence mismatch;
- resync behavior;
- stale snapshot rejection;
- duplicate card IDs;
- partial window catch-up;
- missing update params;
- Thread Detail pagination;
- Thread Detail rehydrate on reconnect and foreground;
- server request and resolution behavior;
- archive action state transitions.

Representative commands:

```bash
rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
```

Interpretation rule: passing Tier B means Swift can handle supplied events. It
does not prove real relay delivery over time.

### Tier C. Relay Integration Tests

Purpose: prove real relay behavior with fake or controlled upstreams.

Coverage required:

- `dock/subscribe` returns canonical snapshot;
- server state mutation emits `dock/update`;
- multi-subscriber updates;
- delete-only delta;
- `dock/resync`;
- Archive mutation emits Dock and Archive convergence;
- live failure fails closed;
- heartbeat is emitted;
- stale snapshot/generation behavior;
- route allow-list rejects unsupported paths.

Representative command:

```bash
rtk npm run test:relay
```

Interpretation rule: passing Tier C proves relay protocol behavior below the UI.
It does not prove the Swift app rendered the update.

### Tier D. Real Relay Client-Path Soak

Purpose: prove long-lived relay streams stay converged with fresh snapshots over
time.

Required properties:

- long-lived `dock/subscribe`;
- periodic fresh `dock/subscribe`;
- comparison of long-lived stream state against fresh snapshot;
- forced `dock/resync`;
- detail probe that runs `thread/read`, full paged `thread/turns/list`, and
  `thread/resume`;
- lag budget;
- retained JSON and Markdown reports.

Representative command family:

```bash
rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs --mode soak --client-path-only --force-dock-resync --max-stream-lag-ms 2000
```

Current doc drift to fix during implementation: older docs mention unsupported
or deleted command surfaces such as `--exhaustive` and deleted parity scripts.
The doc-command gate must make that impossible to miss.

### Tier E. Simulator Displayed-UI Proof

Purpose: prove the iPhone simulator actually displays the live state over time.

Required properties:

- app launched without `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO`;
- real relay-backed or controlled relay-backed rows;
- UI samples over a duration;
- route evidence from relay side;
- row-level and detail-level UI samples;
- transition coverage;
- lag budget;
- retained machine-readable report.

Representative commands:

```bash
rtk make sim-ui-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
rtk make sim-ui-scenario-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
rtk make sim-ui-controlled-scenario-sync-proof SIM='iPhone 17'
rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof SIM='iPhone 17' SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_PASSES=2 MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000
```

Interpretation rule: `CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests` skipping because
`/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-sim-ui-sync-config.json` is absent is not proof.
For update-path changes, this tier must run or be explicitly reported as
blocked by missing simulator/Xcode infrastructure.

### Tier F. Physical Phone Proof

Purpose: prove the real phone path, including network profile and saved host
configuration.

Representative commands:

```bash
rtk make iphone-17-pro
rtk make device-config-verify DEVICE=CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E
rtk make device-logs DEVICE=CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E
```

Interpretation rule: simulator proof is not physical phone proof. Physical
completion requires a real installed app connected through the intended relay
host path.

## Ongoing Cadence

The methodology must run continuously enough to catch drift before manual use.

Recommended cadence:

| Trigger | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| Every source change in update-path files | Tier A plus affected Tier B/C |
| Relay protocol, card DTO, stream, Thread Detail, or proof harness change | Tier A/B/C plus Tier E controlled matrix |
| Daily/nightly on a capable Mac | Tier D soak plus Tier E controlled matrix |
| Before claiming simulator behavior fixed | Tier E on `iPhone 17` |
| Before claiming phone behavior fixed | Tier F |
| Before changing docs/runbooks | Doc-command gate plus affected referenced commands in dry-run or real mode |

Update-path files include:

- `scripts/dock-relay*.mjs`;
- `contract/dock/**`;
- `CodexDock/AppServer/**`;
- `CodexDock/State/**`;
- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/**`;
- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/**`;
- `CodexDockUITests/**`;
- `Makefile`;
- live-update docs and runbooks.

## Proof Acceptance Rules

Every proof report should classify the run as one of:

- `pass`: required routes, transitions, UI samples, freshness states, and lag
  budgets passed.
- `fail`: the proof ran and found divergence, stale UI, missing route evidence,
  missing transition, or lag over budget.
- `blocked`: infrastructure was unavailable, such as no simulator, no relay,
  no app-server, missing signing, or physical device unavailable.
- `outside-contract`: the run used scripted fixtures, debug env vars, preview
  rows, raw app-server path, or another forbidden proof route.

No proof may be counted as pass if:

- it skipped;
- it had no route evidence;
- it only compared static snapshots;
- it lacked a retained report;
- it did not validate its report schema;
- it ignored stale/partial freshness;
- it did not sample over time.

Required retained report fields:

- `schemaVersion`;
- `kind`;
- `startedAt`;
- `endedAt`;
- `durationMs`;
- source host(s);
- app/server/relay build identifiers where available;
- scenario name(s);
- route counts;
- sampled transitions;
- UI sample count;
- max observed lag;
- lag budget;
- freshness states;
- pass/fail findings;
- artifact paths.

## Drift Gates

### Gate 1. Route Registry And Dispatch Parity

The relay dispatch switch, relay route registry/observability config, Swift
route names, and docs must agree.

A route must not be silently valid because a helper auto-created an unregistered
route. New routes are allowed only when they update:

- relay dispatch;
- route registry/observability;
- Swift method constants/DTOs if phone-visible;
- tests;
- docs.

### Gate 2. Schema Version And DTO Parity

These values must move together:

- JSON schema `schemaVersion`;
- relay emitted `schemaVersion`;
- Swift `CodexDockConstants.Dock.streamSchemaVersion`;
- generated Swift DTOs;
- tests and fixtures.

Generated DTO staleness is a build failure, not a review note.

### Gate 3. Executable Doc Commands

Docs that name runnable commands must not drift from real CLIs.

This gate should catch:

- unsupported flags such as stale `--exhaustive`;
- deleted scripts such as stale parity helpers;
- Makefile target renames;
- commands that require env/config but do not say so;
- commands that skip by default while being described as proof.

### Gate 4. Proof Result Schemas

Proof reports need schemas just like card DTOs.

Create and enforce schemas for:

- relay sync audit reports;
- simulator UI sync proof reports;
- controlled simulator fixture reports;
- controlled simulator matrix reports.

The current reports have `schemaVersion` and `kind`, but no schema file guards
their shape. That means proof consumers and docs can drift.

### Gate 5. Heartbeat Contract

If schema, README, Swift tests, or docs say heartbeat exists, relay must emit it.

The gate must fail if:

- heartbeat is documented but not emitted;
- heartbeat is emitted but schema/DTO/tests do not allow it;
- heartbeat marks stale data fresh;
- client does not timeout missing heartbeat.

## UX Freshness Contract

The UI should make these states visible and distinct:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh | Relay has current proof for this view/scope. |
| Partial | Relay has usable rows but incomplete proof/window/source coverage. |
| Stale | Relay has old rows but cannot prove current source state. |
| Reconnecting | Stateful stream/session identity is being rebuilt. |
| Offline | No usable relay path is currently available. |
| Blocked | Command/test/proof could not run because infrastructure is missing. |

Global connectivity may summarize transport reachability, but it must not hide
stale stream freshness. A small "online" badge is misleading if the rows are a
day old.

## Rejected Alternatives

### Static Fixtures As Proof Of Record

Rejected because they prove only merge/render behavior for supplied data. They
do not prove that current Codex work reaches the phone.

### Client-Inferred Recency

Rejected because it creates a second card-truth path and reintroduces ordering
bugs.

### Diagnostics As Freshness

Rejected because route health can be green while the long-lived stream is
unsubscribed or stale.

### New Parallel Test Framework

Rejected because the repo already contains the core live-proof harness. The
right move is to make it mandatory, scheduled, schema-validated, retained, and
drift-gated.

### Invisible Thread Detail Upstream Recovery

Rejected because it is the exact stale-detail failure mode.

### Delete Heartbeat Without Replacement

Rejected because it leaves socket connectivity as the liveness signal. Removing
heartbeat is acceptable only if replaced by an equally strong client-visible
watchdog contract. Making heartbeat real is cleaner because the schema and
Swift already know about it.

### Add `detail/resync` Immediately

Rejected for now because downstream close reuses existing Swift rehydrate
behavior. `detail/resync` is the sanctioned future evolution only if full
evidence shows downstream close is too expensive.

## Implementation Plan Outline

This document does not implement these changes. A future implementation plan
should be phased like this:

1. Update docs/runbooks so command references are executable and this document
   is the canonical live-update architecture reference.
2. Add drift gates that are CI-safe and do not require simulator/device.
3. Make heartbeat real or remove every heartbeat claim and replace it with an
   equivalent explicit watchdog. Consensus recommendation is make heartbeat
   real.
4. Fix stateful recovery: Dock/Archive resubscribe after reconnect and Thread
   Detail upstream recovery closes downstream or triggers sanctioned rehydrate.
5. Add snapshot generation rejection in Swift.
6. Make live failures fail closed in relay freshness.
7. Make Archive reconciliation first-class after archive/unarchive.
8. Add `itemsView:"full"` to Thread Detail history and proof paths, scoped only
   to detail.
9. Add proof-result schemas and validate retained reports.
10. Make update-path changes require the controlled simulator matrix and retain
    reports.
11. Add scheduled soak/matrix runs where infrastructure exists.
12. Add physical phone proof as the completion gate for phone claims.

Each phase must remove or converge old paths. Do not leave a retired side door
alive for tests.

## Canonical Documentation Relationship

This document is the canonical target architecture and ongoing methodology for
live updates.

Relationship to other docs:

- `CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md` remains
  the deep protocol and bug appendix.
- `CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md` remains
  historical evidence for data-contract drift.
- Existing exhaustive sync runbooks/test plans should be updated to remove
  stale commands and align with this methodology.
- README should align with heartbeat reality after implementation.

If another doc disagrees with this target architecture, this doc wins for
live-update architecture intent until a newer explicitly canonical reference
replaces it.

## Final Consensus Statement

Opus 4.8 max and GPT-5.5 xhigh converged on the same architecture:

- one canonical production truth path;
- relay-owned card truth and freshness;
- observable rebuild on stateful identity changes;
- heartbeat as real liveness contract;
- detail history with `itemsView:"full"` only on the detail path;
- live failures fail closed;
- snapshots cannot move state backward;
- Archive is a first-class stream view;
- live proof over time is mandatory, retained, scheduled, schema-validated, and
  gated for update-path changes.

The remaining open value, heartbeat cadence/timeout, is an implementation
parameter. It does not change the architecture.

16	
17	## Bottom Line
18	
19	The architecture is simple: Codex Dock must have one production truth path for
20	live state, and every important claim about freshness must be proven over time.
21	
22	The client must not be asked to guess whether a connected socket means current
23	data. The relay must own app-server decoding, card truth, freshness,
24	completeness, order, and stream liveness. The client renders that truth and
25	requests rebuilds when the relay's stream identity changes or falls behind.
26	
27	The testing strategy is also simple: static snapshots are useful, but they are
28	not proof that the app works. The proof of record is live convergence:
29	
30	```text
31	real or controlled app-server state changes
32	  -> relay projection and subscriptions
33	  -> Swift stream/session clients
34	  -> rendered iPhone UI samples over time
35	  -> retained machine-readable reports with lag budgets
36	```
37	
38	The repo already has much of the live-proof harness. The missing architecture is
39	that this proof is opt-in, unscheduled, ungated, and partly underspecified. That
40	is why stale-update bugs can ship while tests pass.
41	
42	## Canonical Principles
43	
44	### P1. One Owner Per Fact
45	
46	Every client-visible fact has exactly one production owner.
47	
48	| Fact | Canonical owner | Forbidden second owner |
49	| --- | --- | --- |
50	| Dock and Archive card existence | Relay `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams | Swift local metadata, diagnostics, preview fixtures, raw app-server routes |
51	| Card order and recency | Relay `orderKey` / `activityAtMs` | Swift timestamp inference, pins, row text, latest rendered message |
52	| Card freshness and completeness | Relay freshness/completeness fields | Socket connectivity, HTTP diagnostics, host test success |
53	| Human-only filtering | Relay human-started filter, with Swift defensive filter | Client-side list reconstruction from broad raw thread routes |
54	| Thread Detail history | `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus fully paged `thread/turns/list` | Dock cards, raw card summaries, partial resume payloads |
55	| Thread Detail liveness | Focused `thread/resume` session | Socket state alone |
56	| Local labels, rails, pins | Swift local metadata | Relay/card truth fields |
57	
58	Local metadata may decorate visible rows. It must never create a row, change
59	card order, mark data fresh, change status, change summary, or resurrect a row
60	that the relay no longer emits.
61	
62	### P2. Liveness Must Be Re-Proven
63	
64	A connected WebSocket is not proof that the data is current.
65	
66	Every stateful relay-owned stream or session must have an identity:
67	
68	- Dock and Archive streams: `epoch`, `seq`, and `stateGeneration`.
69	- Thread Detail live session: relay downstream session generation plus the
70	  active upstream `thread/resume` binding.
71	- Realtime transcription: transcription `sessionId` plus sequence acceptance.
72	
73	When that identity changes, the missing state must be rebuilt in an observable
74	way:
75	
76	- Dock and Archive must resubscribe or resync.
77	- Thread Detail must rehydrate from history before trusting live deltas again.
78	- The UI must show stale/partial/reconnecting when freshness is not proven.
79	
80	No production path may silently recover a relay upstream session while leaving
81	the phone thinking its old stream is still complete.
82	
83	### P3. Proof Is Over-Time Convergence
84	
85	Proof means the rendered client stays converged with actual source state over a
86	duration and within a lag budget.
87	
88	The following are not enough:
89	
90	- a static fixture that renders once;
91	- a fake Swift stream that manually yields a good payload;
92	- a one-shot `dock/subscribe`;
93	- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, or `/syncz`;
94	- a green `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` when the displayed sync proof
95	  skipped because its config file was absent.
96	
97	Those checks can be useful, but they are lower-tier evidence. They do not prove
98	the live system is current.

100	## Target Architecture
101	
102	### Rule 1. Phone Uses Relay Only
103	
104	The phone connects to the Dock relay on `:4510`, not to the raw authenticated
105	app-server on `:4500`.
106	
107	Allowed normal phone paths:
108	
109	- relay WebSocket for `initialize`, `dock/*`, `archive/*`, Thread Detail,
110	  composer commands, server requests, and transcription;
111	- relay-provided host config such as `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`,
112	  `home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`, LAN hostname, or LAN IP.
113	
114	Forbidden normal phone paths:
115	
116	- raw app-server `:4500`;
117	- raw app-server bearer tokens on device;
118	- phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or broad
119	  state routes used to rebuild cards;
120	- relay SQLite/debug/state routes as card truth.
121	
122	### Rule 2. Relay Owns Card Truth
123	
124	The relay is the only production card-truth owner for Dock and Archive.
125	
126	The relay owns:
127	
128	- app-server history reads;
129	- live loaded-session scans;
130	- human-started filtering;
131	- latest-activity proof;
132	- card normalization;
133	- SQLite materialization;
134	- stream sequence and snapshot generation;
135	- freshness and completeness;
136	- `dock/update` and `archive/update` deltas.
137	
138	Swift owns:
139	
140	- rendering;
141	- grouping/filtering/searching of relay rows;
142	- local decorative metadata;
143	- resync/resubscribe behavior when the relay stream contract says state is
144	  incomplete, stale, mismatched, or behind.
145	
146	Swift must not reconstruct card truth from Thread Detail history or local
147	metadata.
148	
149	### Rule 3. Relay Owns Recency
150	
151	Dock and Archive order are relay-owned. The client renders relay order.
152	
153	The client must not infer row recency from:
154	
155	- latest visible message;
156	- first message;
157	- pinned status;
158	- local label;
159	- local rail;
160	- Thread Detail events;
161	- raw timestamps from a side route.
162	
163	This prevents the same user-facing bug from reappearing under a new local
164	projection.
165	
166	### Rule 4. Thread Detail Uses One History Path
167	
168	Thread Detail history is:
169	
170	```text
171	thread/read includeTurns:false
172	  -> thread/turns/list until nextCursor is empty
173	  -> thread/resume excludeTurns:true
174	```
175	
176	For user-visible detail completeness, `thread/turns/list` must request
177	`itemsView:"full"` on the detail path.
178	
179	Important scoping rule:
180	
181	- Thread Detail history requests should use `itemsView:"full"`.
182	- Relay card-order activity proof calls should not use `itemsView:"full"`.
183	
184	The card-order proof needs turn activity timestamps and ordering proof. It does
185	not need full item bodies. Forcing full item bodies into relay card proof would
186	mix two separate concerns and increase payload cost.
187	
188	Current gap to close during implementation: `ThreadTurnsListParams` does not
189	currently carry `itemsView`, and relay `listThreadTurns` forwards params as-is.
190	The sync audit has a `--turn-items-view` flag, but the production detail path
191	does not currently send the field.
192	
193	### Rule 5. Stateful Recovery Must Be Observable
194	
195	Stateful paths cannot silently reconnect and keep old state.
196	
197	Dock and Archive:
198	
199	- reconnecting the transport is not enough;
200	- `initialize` replay is not enough;
201	- the subscription must be restored;
202	- if subscription continuity is not provable, the stream must resubscribe or
203	  fail into a visible rebuild path.
204	
205	Thread Detail:
206	
207	- if the downstream phone socket closes, Swift already rehydrates;
208	- if the relay loses and recreates the upstream `thread/resume` session, the
209	  phone must also observe a rebuild trigger.
210	
211	Consensus decision: close the downstream Thread Detail socket on relay upstream
212	recovery unless the app-server provides a proven replay guarantee.
213	
214	Why close the downstream socket now:
215	
216	- Swift already has a tested reconnect/rehydrate path.
217	- It avoids adding a new protocol message before the architecture is stable.
218	- It prevents the exact stale-detail failure shape: relay recovered upstream,
219	  phone stayed connected, and missed history was never replayed.
220	
221	Sanctioned future alternative:
222	
223	- a `detail/resync` or equivalent notification may exist later only if it is
224	  `threadId`-stamped, generation-stamped, added to the relay allow-list, added
225	  to Swift DTO handling, added to proof tests, and documented here in the same
226	  change.
227	
228	Until then, invisible upstream recovery is forbidden.
229	
230	### Rule 6. Heartbeat Is Real Contract
231	
232	Heartbeat is not decorative. It is the stream liveness signal.
233	
234	The repo already claims heartbeat in schema, Swift behavior, tests, and README.
235	The target architecture makes it real instead of leaving a dead contract.
236	
237	Relay should emit periodic `kind:"heartbeat"` `dock/update` messages with:
238	
239	- `schemaVersion`;
240	- `view`;
241	- `epoch`;
242	- `seq`;
243	- `stateGeneration`;
244	- `freshness`;
245	- `lastSyncAt` or equivalent freshness timestamp;
246	- no row changes.
247	
248	The client uses heartbeat to detect:
249	
250	- connected-but-unsubscribed streams;
251	- streams whose relay state is stale even though the socket is open;
252	- missing updates beyond a bounded timeout.
253	
254	Heartbeat must never mark failed data fresh. It may keep the transport alive,
255	but freshness remains a relay data claim.
256	
257	Bounded implementation parameter:
258	
259	- heartbeat cadence should align with relay reconcile timing, roughly the
260	  reconcile interval or a small multiple;
261	- client stale timeout should be a small multiple of heartbeat cadence;
262	- exact values belong in constants, not scattered call sites.
263	
264	### Rule 7. Freshness Fails Closed
265	
266	If the relay cannot prove a source is current, client-visible freshness must be
267	stale or partial, not fresh.
268	
269	This applies to:
270	
271	- raw app-server history failures;
272	- live endpoint failures;
273	- live lease scan failures;
274	- validation failures during human-started filtering;
275	- repeated turn cursors;
276	- schema or sequence mismatch;
277	- incomplete windows;
278	- failed archive reconciliation.
279	
280	Current gap to close during implementation: live endpoint failures can be
281	counted and then effectively hidden by history completeness. The target rule is
282	that live-scope probe failure marks the relevant scope stale/incomplete and the
283	client renders that state.
284	
285	### Rule 8. Snapshots Cannot Move State Backward
286	
287	Snapshots are full replacements, but they are not allowed to overwrite newer
288	state with older state.
289	
290	The relay already has monotonic stream sequence material:
291	
292	- `seq`;
293	- `stateGeneration`;
294	- `epoch`;
295	- `schemaVersion`.
296	
297	Swift must reject stale compatible snapshots when their generation is older
298	than the current host/view state. A compatible schema is not enough.
299	
300	Current gap to close during implementation: Swift currently applies compatible
301	snapshots without a stale-generation guard.
302	
303	### Rule 9. Archive Is A First-Class View
304	
305	Archive and Dock are separate views with related but distinct freshness.
306	
307	Archive/unarchive mutations must reconcile and publish both affected views:
308	
309	- Dock view;
310	- Archive view.
311	
312	Archive freshness must not be accidentally coupled to Dock freshness such that
313	one scope can stale or freshen the other without proof.
314	
315	Current gap to close during implementation: archive mutation scheduling is
316	drift-prone because the mutation ingestion path schedules generic reconciliation
317	but does not make Archive convergence a first-class invariant.
